items.title: Uncertainty analysis: bounded-error data confine the parameter of a $C^1$ prediction along a declared unit direction in $\mathbb R^n$
items.reference: completed-expansion-arguments.md#U1; primary accounts E1-E3 impose no unstated sampling law
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $\theta_0\in U$, and let $u\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfy $\lVert u\rVert_2=1$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval with $0\in I$ and such that $\gamma(\theta):=\theta_0+\theta u\in U$ for every $\theta\in I$. Let $F:U\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $F(\theta_0)=0$, and suppose that for every $\theta\in I$ the directional derivative of $F$ along $u$ satisfies
$$D_uF(\theta_0+\theta u)=\langle\nabla F(\theta_0+\theta u),u\rangle\ge m>0$$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]], [[thm-gradient-represents-directional-derivatives-and-steepest-ascent]]). Let a recorded scalar $\hat y\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $|\hat y|\le s$ with $s\ge0$, and let a calibration-error bound $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$ with $\delta\ge0$ hold for $y:=F(\theta_0+\theta u)$ at a candidate $\theta\in I$. Then
$$|\theta|\le\frac{s+\delta}{m},$$
and the corresponding configuration displacement $\gamma(\theta)-\theta_0=\theta u$ has Euclidean length $\lVert\theta u\rVert_2=|\theta|$. The conclusion is a deterministic conditional statement about the stated bounds; it is not a sampling law, a statistical inference, or a claim about any historical report, and the parameters $s,\delta,m$ are supplied by the user of the statement rather than estimated from data here.
items.strategy: Set $\gamma(\theta):=\theta_0+\theta u$ and $g:=F\circ\gamma:I\to\mathbb R$, and verify the hypotheses of the bounded-error model-comparison lemma for $g$ on $I$ before reading off its conclusion. (i) Each component $\theta\mapsto(\theta_0)_j+\theta u_j$ of $\gamma$ is a sum of a constant and a scalar multiple of the identity $\theta\mapsto\theta^1$, hence differentiable with derivative $u_j$ ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). These partial derivatives are the constant functions $u_j$, so they exist on the open interval $I$ and are continuous there; [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]] therefore makes $\gamma$ totally differentiable at every $\theta\in I$ with $D\gamma(\theta)$ the linear map whose matrix is $J\gamma(\theta)$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), that is, $D\gamma(\theta)(h)=hu$ for $h\in\mathbb R$. (ii) Both $F$ (on the open set $U$) and $\gamma$ (on the open interval $I$) are covered by the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]), so $g$ is totally differentiable at every $\theta\in I$ with $Dg(\theta)=DF(\gamma(\theta))\circ D\gamma(\theta)$. For a real-valued function on an open subset of $\mathbb R$ the ordinary derivative is the total derivative applied to $1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), so $g'(\theta)=DF(\gamma(\theta))(u)=D_uF(\gamma(\theta))=\langle\nabla F(\gamma(\theta)),u\rangle\ge m$ by the hypothesis ([[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], [[thm-gradient-represents-directional-derivatives-and-steepest-ascent]]). (iii) The derivative $g'=\sum_j(\partial_jF\circ\gamma)\,u_j$ is continuous on $I$: the partial derivatives $\partial_jF$ are continuous on $U$ because $F$ is $C^1$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]); $\gamma$ is continuous because $d_2(\gamma(\theta),\gamma(\theta'))=\lVert(\theta-\theta')u\rVert_2=|\theta-\theta'|$ by the homogeneity of the Euclidean norm and $\lVert u\rVert_2=1$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], [[def-metric-continuity]]); each composite $\partial_jF\circ\gamma$ is then continuous because for open $V\subseteq\mathbb R$ its preimage is $\gamma^{-1}[\partial_jF^{-1}[V]]$, the preimage under $\gamma$ of an open set ([[thm-metric-continuity-characterisations]]); and $g'$ is a finite sum of scalar multiples of these composite functions, hence continuous as a real function on $I$ ([[lem-real-and-metric-notions-agree]], [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]]). Thus $g$ is $C^1$ on $I$ in the lemma's sense, and $g(0)=F(\theta_0)=0$. (iv) Apply the bounded-error model-comparison lemma ([[lem-em-bounded-error-model-comparison]]) to $g$ on $I$ with lower bound $m>0$ and centre $0$: every candidate $\theta\in I$ whose model value $y=g(\theta)=F(\theta_0+\theta u)$ satisfies $|\hat y|\le s$ and $|y-\hat y|\le\delta$ obeys $|\theta-0|\le(s+\delta)/m$. Finally $\lVert\theta u\rVert_2=|\theta|\,\lVert u\rVert_2=|\theta|$ by homogeneity of the Euclidean norm and $\lVert u\rVert_2=1$ ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). No probability model, sampling law or statistical inference is used at any step.

references.title: J. Lebl, Basic Analysis I: Introduction to Real Analysis, Volume I (open textbook), Chapter 4 'The Derivative', §4.1.1-§4.2.5, printed pp. 154-168, version 6.3 (May 15, 2026)

G. L. Luke, Notes of lectures on Multivariable Calculus (University of Oxford course notes hosted at people.maths.ox.ac.uk/~tillmann), §2 'The Total Derivative', §3 'Properties of Total Derivatives', §7 'Mean Value Theorem', PDF pp. 5-6, 9-13

items.title: Sharpness of the bounded-error uncertainty bound for a linear prediction, and failure once the response lower bound is dropped
items.statement:
Identify $\mathbb R$ with $\mathbb R^1$ by $t\mapsto(t)$, the function on $\{0\}$ with value $t$. This bijection preserves distances because $\lVert(t)-(r)Vert_2=|t-r|$; the symbols $u=1$ and $
abla F=m$ below use this identification.

(i) Specialise [[thm-em-uncertainty-analysis]] to $n=1$, $U=\mathbb R$, $	heta_0=0$, $u=1$, $I=\mathbb R$ and $F(	heta)=m	heta$ with $m>0$. Then $F$ is $C^1$, $F(0)=0$, $
abla F(	heta)=m$ and $\langle
abla F(	heta),1angle=m\ge m$, so the theorem's hypothesis holds with equality. Fix the recorded value $\hat y=0$ (so $s=0$) and any $\delta\ge0$. A candidate $	heta\in\mathbb R$ is compatible with the calibration bound exactly when $|F(	heta)-\hat y|=|m	heta|\le\delta$, that is, exactly when $|	heta|\le\delta/m$; this is precisely the theorem's bound $(s+\delta)/m=\delta/m$, and the bound is attained (equality) at $	heta=\pm\delta/m$. Hence the constant $(s+\delta)/m$ cannot be improved for this instance, and the special case $\delta=0$ leaves $	heta=0$ as the only compatible candidate. (ii) The positive lower bound on the response is not removable. If it is dropped, take $m=0$ and $F\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R$: the hypothesis $\langle
abla F(	heta),uangle\ge m>0$ fails, and with the same data $\hat y=0$, $s=0$, $\delta\ge0$ every $	heta\in\mathbb R$ is compatible, because $y=0$ and $|y-\hat y|=0\le\delta$; no finite parameter bound then follows from the indicator and the two bounds alone. (iii) These are mathematical observations about a hypothetical bounded-error model: no experimental data, sampling law or statistical inference is used or asserted, and the displayed numbers are stipulated parameters, not measurements.
items.strategy:
(i) The derivative of $F(	heta)=m	heta$ is $F'(	heta)=m$: the identity $	heta\mapsto	heta^1$ has derivative $1$ and scalar multiples inherit the scaled derivative ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). With $n=1$ the gradient is the derivative, $
abla F(	heta)=(m)$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), and the pairing with $u=1$ is $\langle
abla F(	heta),1angle=m\cdot1=m$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]); also $F(0)=0$ and $\lVert uVert_2=1$, so every hypothesis of the theorem is met. Multiplying the inequality $|	heta|\le\delta/m$ by $m>0$ gives $|m	heta|\le\delta$ and conversely, using $|m	heta|=m|	heta|$ and the defining clauses of the absolute value ([[lem-of-abs-value]], [[def-abs-value]]); at $	heta=\pm\delta/m$ one has $|m	heta|=\delta$, so equality holds in the bound while the candidate remains compatible; and for $\delta=0$ the inequality $|m	heta|\le0$ forces $m	heta=0$, hence $	heta=0$. (ii) For $F\equiv0$ the gradient vanishes ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), so $\langle
abla F(	heta),uangle=0$ is not $\ge m$ for any $m>0$ and the theorem's hypothesis is not met; nevertheless $y=F(	heta)=0=\hat y$ for every $	heta$, so $|y-\hat y|=0\le\delta$ and $|\hat y|=0\le s$ hold for every $	heta\in\mathbb R$: the data cannot confine the parameter at all. (iii) The comparisons are order arithmetic in $\mathbb R$ on stipulated quantities; no probabilistic or empirical claim is made ([[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-abs-value]]).
